palmer_gloss: The salt-pan. See Memoirs under 'Manahath' and 'Manocho'.
memoirs: Memoirs III p. 21: Malhah = Manocho of the LXX (Josh 15:59 add.) and probably biblical Manahath; rock-cut tombs east of the village. Memoirs III p. 136: cave El Medbah SW of village; cave Umm Babein NE; 'On the east is a tomb with six kokim and an outer chamber'; Clermont-Ganneau: approaches 'filled with tombs cut in the rock'.
region: Jerusalem (c. 5 km SW of the Temple Mount; village of al-Maliha)
known: Arabic name already used for Manahath/Manocho (Memoirs III p. 21) and Talmudic Malkhaya (Schwarz, cited Memoirs III p. 136-137). No Copper Scroll link found in the shared files or this pass.
verdict: NEW, weak-to-low. Only candidate where sound (exact m-l-ḥ in Arabic script) and a Jerusalem-area setting with a kokhim tomb and caves coincide; but the Arabic word is an ordinary appellative ('salty/salt-pan'), the name is already claimed by Manahath, and Milik/Puech read ha-Melaḥ inside the Temple area. Elitzur condition (i) fails: no ancient source fixes a Melaḥ near Jerusalem.

palmer_gloss: The pool of Harb. p.n.; meaning 'battle' or 'a spear'.
memoirs: Not found in Memoirs III OCR (searched 'Harb').
region: Jericho W (SWP square Os: ʿAin ed-Duk, ʿAin el-Qelt, Deir el-Qelt)
known: Milik/Puech: Ḥorebbeh = monastery of Chorembe near Kh. el-Mafjar [readings.json e1-ruin]
verdict: NEW, low. Exact ḥ-r-b in Arabic script and a pool in the Jericho square, but Ḥarb is a common Arabic personal/tribal name (Palmer: p.n.) and the scroll word is most likely the common noun 'ruin'. Location within the square not fixed.

palmer_name: Hŭrubbet el-Ḥaṭṭâbeh (also Hŭrubbet Abu Selhûb, Hŭrubbet Umm el-Kuleib, Herâbi el-Beid, Herubbet es-Sûk)
palmer_gloss: The cistern of the firewood carriers / The white cisterns.
memoirs: Memoirs III Appendix p. 439: 'The well of Sûk or Tzuk (Bîr es Sûk or Herubbet es Sûk) ... every appearance of antiquity, with a small aqueduct ... covering the rock-cut cistern'.
region: Judean desert east of Jerusalem and Bethlehem–Tekoa
verdict: LEXICAL LEAD, low-medium. Palmer records a local word hurubbeh/herâbi = 'cistern' in exactly the Judean-desert zone. If 3Q15's חרובא (I 1) is this word rather than 'little ruin', entry 1 would read 'in the cistern in the Valley of Achor, under the steps going east' — a stepped cistern. Obstacle: Arabic writes ه (h), Hebrew has ח (ḥ). Needs a dialect dictionary check (etymology of hurubbeh) before use.

palmer_name: ʿAin el-Qelt / Wâdy el-Qelt / Deir el-Qelt
palmer_gloss: The spring of the mountain hollow or tarn.
memoirs: Memoirs III list of illustrations: 'Wady Kelt — Plan of aqueduct'; 'Aqueducts near Jericho'.
region: Jericho W (Wadi Qelt; same square as Choziba/entry 32)
known: Not proposed in the shared files; proposals are Tell es-Sultan (Puech), Carmel (Milik), Transjordan (Goranson), ʿEin Samiya (Zissu 2001, PEQ 133:145-158), unidentified (Eshel)
verdict: NEW, low. In Palmer's Latin it scores 0.86, but in Arabic script it needs kaf→qāf and loss of medial ḥet, two irregular steps; qalt is an ordinary Arabic noun ('rock pool'). Geography (aqueducts, pools near Jericho) is compatible with Puech's Jericho hypothesis but adds no independent anchor.

memoirs: Memoirs III p. 303: 'A small village on a ridge, built of stone, with a well to the south. Apparently an ancient place, with rock-cut tombs.'
region: Hebron hills (NW of Hebron) — outside all proposed Koḥlit areas
known: Not proposed in the shared files
verdict: NEW, low. Exact root k-ḥ-l in Arabic script (best sound match for Koḥlit in the whole list), with rock-cut tombs (cf. entry 60 'tombs at its mouth'); but kaḥḥāl/kuḥl is an ordinary Arabic word, the feminine -it is missing, and nothing ties Koḥlit to the Hebron hills.

palmer_gloss: The house of the T'âmirah Arabs.
memoirs: Memoirs III pp. 29-30: 'A small village on a hill with wells and a few olives. The name is that of an Arab tribe which was originally settled in the place.'
region: E of Bethlehem, near Herodium — inside Puech's Tekoa–Herodium sector for entries 39-45
known: Milik: Beth Tamar near Gibeah; Puech objects (no gorge) [readings.json e43-bet-tamar]
verdict: NEW, low. Location fits Puech's sector and lies near ʿAin en-Naṭuf (entry 38), but the Arabic has an extra ʿayn (root ʿ-m-r) and Palmer and the Memoirs give it as a Bedouin tribal name. Probably coincidence.

region: W of Jerusalem (village of ʿAqqur), c. 30 km from Jericho
known: Achor placed NE of Jericho (Milik, Puech) or in the Buqeiʿa (Allegro, Eshel)
verdict: REJECT as Achor: wrong region for the biblical Achor (Judah's northern border near Jericho); Arabic qāf for Hebrew kaf; ʿaqūr is the Arabic cognate of Hebrew ʿaqar 'barren', not of ʿakor.

palmer_gloss: The gate to the paths. The cross roads west of Bethlehem on the road to Bâb Jâla.
known: Sekakah = Kh. Qumran (Puech), Wadi Qumran (Milik 1960), Kh. es-Samra (Milik 1962; Cross & Milik)
verdict: REJECT: exact s-k-k but an Arabic common noun (sikak 'paths'), at a road junction far from the Judean-desert setting of Sekakah.
REJECT: qāf for kaf twice, and in Samaria, far outside the 'wilderness' town lists (Josh 15:61) and the scroll's Jericho–Sekakah route (V 13).
REJECT: artefact of Latin transliteration; Arabic ṣ-q-ʿ ≠ s-k-k.

scroll_name: Valley of Zered (Wolters' reading of X 8)
known: Puech/Milik read the valley of Job (Bîr Ayyûb)
verdict: REJECT: OCR artefact (both OCRs read 'Zerd'; the page has Zerʿ, ع).

palmer_gloss: The caves of the familiar ones.
verdict: REJECT: Arabic participle of the root ʾ-n-s ('familiar'), not m-n-s; and Manos may not be a name at all.

palmer_name: Mellâḥet Rusheidîyeh / Mellâḥet Umm Ehdeib; el-Malḥah (XXI)
palmer_gloss: The salt pond of the Rusheideh (Arabs) / The salt.
region: N shore of the Dead Sea near the Jordan mouth; desert E of Tekoa
verdict: REJECT as name survival: descriptive Arabic words for salt pans (cognate translation), exactly what Elitzur's rule discounts.
REJECT: Arabic tāʾ for Hebrew ṭet; ordinary noun; entry is a Temple court.
